In the current SCOPe release (2.08, stable; latest periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16) PA1492 has been moved into the flavodoxin-like fold and into the same superfamily as the deoxyribosyltransferase, c.23.14, as a separate family. The relationship therefore went from 'same class only' (no asserted structural similarity, no asserted homology) to 'same superfamily' (probable common ancestry, but not the same family).

Verified SCOPe facts, release 1.69:
- PA1492 domains d1t1ja_ (sunid 106249) and d1t1jb_ (sunid 106250), whole chains A and B, sccs c.137.1.1. Lineage: class c 'Alpha and beta proteins (a/b)' (sunid 51349) > fold c.137 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110459) > superfamily c.137.1 (sunid 110460) > family c.137.1.1 (sunid 110461) > protein 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110462) > species Pseudomonas aeruginosa (sunid 110463). PA1492 was thus the sole member of its own fold, superfamily and family.
- Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase domains d1f8ya_ (sunid 31395) and d1f8yb_ (sunid 31396), sccs c.23.14.1. Lineage: class c > fold c.23 'Flavodoxin-like' (sunid 52171) > superfamily c.23.14 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52309) > family c.23.14.1 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52310) > protein 'Nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase' (sunid 52311) > species Lactobacillus leichmannii (sunid 52312).
- Lowest shared node in 1.69: class c only. Different folds, so SCOP 1.69 made no positive homology (or even fold-similarity) assertion between them.

Verified SCOPe facts, release 2.08 (current):
- PA1492 is now d1t1ja1 (sunid 106249, 1t1j A:1-118) and d1t1jb1 (sunid 106250, B:1-118), sccs c.23.14.2. Lineage: class c > fold c.23 'Flavodoxin-like' (sunid 52171) > superfamily c.23.14, now renamed 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like' (sunid 52309) > family c.23.14.2 'Hypothetical protein PA1492' (sunid 110461) > protein (sunid 110462) > species Pseudomonas aeruginosa [TaxId: 287] (sunid 110463). Limits: (1) Shared superfamily supports common ancestry but does not justify transferring the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase function, substrate or catalytic mechanism to PA1492, which is still annotated as a hypothetical structural-genomics protein. (2) 1f8y is not an interchangeable structural template for PA1492 at the family level; any modelling would need an inspected alignment. (3) The 1.69 placement in different folds was not a claim of non-homology, and the 2.08 placement should not be read as a claim that the two are as closely related as members of one family. (4) No periodic-update-specific changes beyond the 2.08 stable data were examined.

Interpretation (evolutionary strength): Moving PA1492 from a singleton fold into superfamily c.23.14 is a positive homology assertion by the SCOP curators: SCOPe now treats PA1492 and the Lactobacillus nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase as probable descendants of a common ancestor. Because they are kept in distinct families (c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1), SCOPe does not assert the close, usually sequence-detectable relationship that a shared family implies. The superfamily renaming from 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase' to 'N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like' reflects that the superfamily now contains members beyond the characterised enzyme family. Andreeva et al. 2008 (SCOP 1.73 paper) cite this as an example of a previously isolated fold being merged into an existing superfamily once a remote relationship was recognised; the API responses confirm the net 1.69-to-2.08 change but the exact intermediate release in which the merge occurred (e.g. 1.71 or 1.73) was not queried, and the structural/sequence rationale for the merge is not exposed by the API and so is not verified here.

Limits: (1) Shared superfamily supports common ancestry but does not justify transferring the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase function, substrate or catalytic mechanism to PA1492, which is still annotated as a hypothetical structural-genomics protein. (2) 1f8y is not an interchangeable structural template for PA1492 at the family level; any modelling would need an inspected alignment. (3) The 1.69 placement in different folds was not a claim of non-homology, and the 2.08 placement should not be read as a claim that the two are as closely related as members of one family.
